content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

**What I checked.** The AUDIT rule targets audit, inspection or verification rights that *bind us*. I ran independent searches across the whole document for "audit", "inspect", "examine records", "verification", "books and records", "records", "access", "normal business hours", "reasonable notice", and for any right running from the Servicer toward the Issuer/Depositor.

**Result.** The term "audit" appears nowhere. Only two review clauses exist, and both run **in our favour**:

- **Section 3.6 (p0131)** — the *Servicer* (Cellco, our counterparty) must give the Issuer, Depositor, Parent Support Provider, Administrator, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee access to its records to review the Servicer's performance.
- **Section 3.9(e) (p0146)** — the *Custodian* (also Cellco) must give the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems.

The remaining hits point the same direction: p0437 (Servicer delivers records to the Administrator/Issuer for Regulation AB) and p0446–p0447 (Servicer grants the Asset Representations Reviewer access, best-efforts redaction of PII).

Cellco holds **no** reciprocal right to audit or access our records or systems. So no walk-away trigger (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) is present, and there is no counterparty audit right for the frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost-allocation or no-system-access parameters to attach to. Flagging here would mean redlining a clause that benefits us, which the playbook forbids.

**Two points noted in the rationale, deliberately not flagged.** The planner asked whether the policy qualifiers gut our access — our review rights are "subject to the Servicer's security, confidentiality and privacy policies," and Section 3.6 further requires access "by all parties at the same time" at the Servicer's offices. Both weaken *our own* inspection rights rather than imposing anything on us, so they sit outside this rule's checklist, which only caps audits against the Customer. Strengthening our access would need to be raised under a separate audit-rights-in-our-favour position; I did not stretch AUDIT to cover it, since its atomic elements are all Vendor-constraining and none could be honestly mapped.

Because the finding is compliant, I did not call `propose_redline` and submitted no element coverage.
